answer: Each maker draws one measure of judged work per epoch from the oasis, and the oasis splits that measure across every cedar the maker grows, so the rings of every cedar fill that much slower. An honest newcomer draws the whole measure, filling one cedar. To weigh the same as one honest cedar, each clone must accumulate N times the epochs of work it judges itself, N being the head count of its own maker, and N clones take N times the elapsed epochs since the measure never widens. The maker's dune tallies its cedar, so a fresh purse inherits no rings.
